content.text: Line 59 has `bi < |b| - 1` instead of `bi < |b|`, which weakens it so the sortedness invariant can't be preserved when appending `a[ai]` while `bi == |b|-1`.

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "preservation",
 "diagnosis": "The invariant at line 59 was weakened to 'bi < |b| - 1', so it says nothing about the last element of b. When bi == |b|-1 and the loop appends a[ai] (because a[ai] <= b[bi]), nothing relates the previous last output element to b[bi], and after an append of b[bi] in the next step sortedness (line 60) cannot be proven. The guard should be 'bi < |b|' to mirror the invariant for a."}
EOF
sed -i 's/bi < (|b|) - 1 ==>/bi < |b| ==>/' program.dfy && sed -n 59p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
Fixed: `program.dfy` now verifies (4 verified, 0 errors).

**What was wrong:** The loop invariant on line 59 in `merge` had a weakened guard, `bi < |b| - 1`. Because of that, it said nothing about the last element of `b`. Suppose `bi == |b|-1` and the loop appends from `a`. Then the verifier had no fact linking the last element of `output` to `b[bi]`. When `b[bi]` was appended in the next step, it could not prove the sortedness invariant on line 60, which is where the error was reported. This was a failure to maintain the invariant (preservation).

**The fix:** I changed the guard to `bi < |b|`, so it now matches the invariant for `a` on line 58:
```dafny
invariant 0 < |output| && bi < |b| ==> output[|output|-1] <= b[bi]
```

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before making the edit. It records `invariant` / `preservation` with this explanation.
